title: Euclidean Geometry
summary: Properties of special quadrilaterals, proving that a quadrilateral is a parallelogram, and the midpoint theorem and its converse, with reasons in geometry proofs.

items: Angles on a straight line add up to $180^\circ$ (∠s on a str line).
Vertically opposite angles are equal (vert opp ∠s).
Parallel lines: corresponding ∠s are equal; alternate ∠s are equal; co-interior ∠s add up to $180^\circ$.
Angles in a triangle add up to $180^\circ$ (sum of ∠s in △); the exterior ∠ of a △ equals the sum of the interior opposite ∠s.
Congruent triangles: SSS, SAS, AAS, RHS.

rows: Both pairs of opposite sides parallel and equal; opposite angles equal; diagonals bisect each other
A parallelogram with four right angles; diagonals equal
A parallelogram with four equal sides; diagonals bisect each other at right angles and bisect the angles
A rectangle and a rhombus: all sides equal, all angles $90^\circ$, diagonals equal and perpendicular
At least one pair of opposite sides parallel
Two pairs of adjacent sides equal; diagonals perpendicular; one diagonal bisects the other

notes.text: Proving a quadrilateral is a parallelogram
A quadrilateral is a parallelogram if **any one** of these is true:

items: Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel (definition).
Both pairs of opposite sides are equal.
Both pairs of opposite angles are equal.
One pair of opposite sides is both equal and parallel.

notes.label: Midpoint theorem
notes.text: The line segment joining the midpoints of two sides of a triangle is **parallel** to the third side and **half** its length. (Reason: midpt theorem)

notes.label: Converse
notes.text: A line drawn through the midpoint of one side of a triangle, **parallel** to a second side, bisects the third side. (Reason: line through midpt ∥ to 2nd side)

notes.title: Worked example 1
notes.problem: In △ABC, D and E are the midpoints of AB and AC. If BC = 14 cm and $\hat{B} = 65^\circ$, find DE and $\hat{ADE}$.
steps: DE ∥ BC (midpt theorem), so $\hat{ADE} = \hat{B} = 65^\circ$ (corresp ∠s; DE ∥ BC).

notes.title: Worked example 2: a proof
notes.problem: P, Q, R and S are the midpoints of the sides AB, BC, CD and DA of quadrilateral ABCD. Prove that PQRS is a parallelogram.
steps: In △ABC: PQ ∥ AC and PQ = ½AC (midpt theorem).
In △ADC: SR ∥ AC and SR = ½AC (midpt theorem).
So PQ ∥ SR and PQ = SR.
∴ PQRS is a parallelogram (one pair of opp sides = and ∥).

notes.label: Exam tip
notes.text: Every statement in a geometry proof needs a **reason** in brackets. Use the accepted abbreviations, e.g. (alt ∠s; AB ∥ CD), (opp sides of ∥m), (midpt theorem).

questions.prompt: In parallelogram ABCD, $\hat{A} = 2x + 30^\circ$ and $\hat{B} = x$. Find $x$ and $\hat{C}$, with reasons.
In △PQR, M and N are the midpoints of PQ and PR. MN = 6 cm and $\hat{PMN} = 72^\circ$. Find QR and $\hat{Q}$, with reasons.
questions.memo:
✓ QR = 12 cm (midpt theorem) (1)
✓ MN ∥ QR (midpt theorem) (1)
✓ $\hat{Q} = 72^\circ$ (corresp ∠s; MN ∥ QR) (1)

questions.prompt: In △ABC, D is the midpoint of AB. A line through D parallel to BC meets AC at E. If AE = 5 cm and DE = 4 cm, find EC and BC, with reasons.
questions.memo:
✓ E is the midpoint of AC (line through midpt ∥ to 2nd side) (1)
✓ EC = 5 cm (1)
✓ DE = ½BC (midpt theorem) (1)
✓ BC = 8 cm (1)
